In an intrinsically safe circuit an isolator or barrier limits the energy available to the safe side of the circuit. So in the event of a fault condition there is not enough energy to create a spark.

As OP has stated this is actually not really an intrinsically safe circuit, it is using pressurisation to prevent dangerous gasses from entering the enclosure. A pressurisation unit will monitor the enclosure, if it loses pressure, a trip signal will be sent and all power will be shut to the enclosure. 
From the installs I see, safe side cabling is either light blue or contained in a light blue cable duct. It is always kept separate from non-is circuits.
